gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the UGREEN Nexode 200W 4-port (its best-value 100 W + 100 W pick) comes in two versions. The 2025 launch unit (ASIN B0DG91Q6YD, whose manual ChatGPT got) drew reports of inconsistent power and high temperatures. UGREEN then shipped an 'optimized' revision (Europe, February 2026; US ASIN B0G7HZT7DN, May 2026) with the same 140/100/30 W USB-C ports, the same finish and the same size, and no published marking that tells the two apart.
standout_why: I compared against the cited rival pages: anker.com A2683 and A2345, Satechi's ST-C200GM-US manual, Satechi's ChargeView 240W power-distribution and power-sharing articles, Macworld's Anker Prime 250W review, and computingforgeeks.com (Real Port Splits), plus manuals.plus B0DG91Q6YD and our own page. Between them they already cover which port pairs give 100 W + 100 W and the e-marked-cable rule. ChatGPT already told shoppers to use C1 + C2 on the UGREEN, the Satechi pair table was cited, and ChargeView's 100/100/40 W three-device split was cited. None of them mentions that the UGREEN 4-port was revised, or the reports of inconsistent power on the first version. The manuals.plus PDF ChatGPT got belongs to the original ASIN. Rivals also leave out the exact port exclusions on the six-port units: Satechi's PD5/PD6 and ChargeView's C5/C6 cap at 20 W and 30 W, so plugging a laptop there breaks 100 W + 100 W.
decides: This backs the Anker Prime 200W (A2683) as the cleanest pick. It is $69.99 and in stock on anker.com today, any two of its four USB-C ports give up to 100 W each, and Anker's only condition is e-marked cables. The UGREEN 4-port's 100 W + 100 W works only on C1 + C2 (C3 is a 30 W port), and a buyer should try to get the revised listing (B0G7HZT7DN), not the 2025 unit. Satechi's 200W and ChargeView 240W suit buyers who want a choice of ports: four 100 W-capable ports, plus 140 W + 100 W on the ChargeView, as long as neither laptop goes into the two low-power ports.

findings.source_title: New upgraded Ugreen 200W 4-port Charger coming to US (Notebookcheck, Polly Allcock, 2026-05-11)

findings.label: Which ports give 100 W + 100 W
findings.value: Only the first two USB-C ports (C1 140 W max, C2 100 W); C3 is 30 W max, USB-A 22.5 W
findings.source_title: New upgraded Ugreen 200W 4-port Charger coming to US (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Notebookcheck: 'use the first two USB-C outputs to charge a pair of laptops at 100W each.' I couldn't open UGREEN's US page (HTTP 429).

findings.label: Port pairs for 100 W + 100 W and cable condition
findings.value: Any two of the four USB-C ports: 'each can deliver up to 100W max'; 'For 100W output, use E-Marker chip cables'; USB-A ports 22.5 W max
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (200W, 6 Ports, GaN) - Anker US
findings.note: Anker lists 200 W total with 2 to 4 ports in use and 199 W with 5 or 6. Its page contradicts itself on whether an AC cord is included ('AC Cable Not Included' vs 'use the provided AC cord'). A replacement must be a C7 2-pin cord rated above 3.2 A.

findings.value: PD1/PD2: PD 3.1, 20 V 5 A and 28 V 5 A, 140 W max; PD3/PD4: PD 3.0, 20 V 5 A, 100 W max; PD5/PD6: 20 W max

findings.label: Two-port pairs
findings.value: C1 + C2/C3/C4 = 140 W + 100 W; C2+C3, C2+C4, C3+C4 = 100 W + 100 W; any pair with C5 or C6 drops that port to 30 W; six ports = 70/70/30/30/20/20 W
findings.source_title: Power Distribution - ChargeView 240W Desktop Charger | ST-C6CV240C-US – Satechi
findings.note: AVS on C1/C2 for MacBooks that take more than 100 W. The page gives no cable requirement.

findings.label: Port limits, cable rule and firmware caveat
findings.value: C1 only for 140 W (cable rated 140 W or higher); C2–C4 100 W each; two ports in use up to 240 W total; 'OTA upgrades or different firmware versions may cause variations in power distribution'; $149.99, in stock
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (250W, 6 Ports, GaNPrime) - Anker US
findings.note: Anker publishes no pair table. 140 W + 100 W on C1 + one of C2–C4 is my inference from the per-port maximums. The 16-inch MacBook Pro M1/M2 needs USB-C-to-MagSafe for 140 W; the M3 accepts USB-C to USB-C.
